svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Activate the expired fixture only in this lab
Application server (TLS-APP01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.10
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-app01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
sudo test -f /root/tls-rollbacks/after-renewal.conf && scp learner@10.90.0.20:~/tls-ca/public/app-
expired.crt ~/tls-work/app-expired.crt
cat ~/tls-work/app-expired.crt ~/tls-work/intermediate.crt > ~/tls-work/app-expired-fullchain.pem
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0644 ~/tls-work/app-expired-fullchain.pem /etc/pki/tls/certs/app-
expired-fullchain.pem
sudo restorecon -v /etc/pki/tls/certs/app-expired-fullchain.pem
sudo sed -i -E 's@ssl_certificate .*;@ssl_certificate /etc/pki/tls/certs/app-expired-
fullchain.pem;@; s@ssl_certificate_key .*;@ssl_certificate_key /etc/pki/tls/private/app-v1.key;@'
/etc/nginx/conf.d/app-tls.conf
sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx
openssl s_client -connect 10.90.0.10:443 -servername app.example.mil -CAfile ~/tls-work/root.crt
-verify_return_error -verify_hostname app.example.mil < /dev/null
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
The client reports certificate has expired. NGINX may remain active because expiry is a client
validation failure.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Confirm the safe v3 baseline exists. Copy the expired public leaf from the CA and assemble its chain.
2. Install the fixture and change both directives to expired chain plus app-v1.key. Version 1 is
intentional: this fixture was signed from app-v1.csr.
3. Notice that nginx -t can succeed for an expired but structurally valid pair. Reload only to create
this isolated final-lab condition, never on a real service.
4. Run the verification command. It must now fail with expiration; the practice Firefox profile should
also warn. Do not click through it.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
